subject: Loading reversed when fitted to samples of the same population

messages.author: a8144d65f36aaf6a
messages.subject: Loading reversed when fitted to samples of the same population
parts:
Hi Phil,

I am fitting the same graded model to multiple (100) samples of a population, and want to compare the loadings of items by plotting the density of loadings of the 100 populations and comparing those densities. This is how the loadings look like for a factor on which all items load:


I do not expect these distributions (small mean and large SD). When I plot a parallel plot of the loadings, it shows that for some samples the loadings have been reversed (almost 20/100 of the samples clearly have revere loadings for the first 4 items):

Is there any way to prevent/remedy this? (I would rather fix it with the models I already have fitted since this processed has been repeated for 9 different models on 30 different datasets, and it's pretty time consuming to redo!)

Thanks in advance,
MH Manuel.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Loading reversed when fitted to samples of the same population
parts:
You should be able to just modify the starting values via the three-step mod2values() to make the model converge more towards the orientation you want. Latent variable models will fit exactly the same if some/all of the loads are reversed, so you probably want the optimizer to stay way form this behaviour. I don't know what kind of model you are running (EFA vs CFA, or the itemtypes), but that's the general strategy.

Phil
